texte: But there was a plot twist. Something completely unexpected. Borrowing against unrealized gains is actually more prevalent among the middle class. In 2022, Americans in the 50th-90th percentile borrowed against 42% of their unrealized gains, primarily through their homes. Regular families were taking out debt against the paper equity of their own homes. It wasn’t the normal practice of the ultra wealthy. It was a more extreme way of life for a smaller group: the people who had almost their entire wealth invested in a single stock, bought office towers with 5-year loans, and or used a credit line like a checking account.
